scope: offline static ARM32 Thumb disassembly of the recovered Windows Mobile Origa2Auth.sys

wdf_bind_info.interpretation: Embedded WDF_BIND_INFO v1 metadata identifies the driver target as KMDF 1.15; this permits matching slots against the 1.15 enum.

system_hive_correlation.interpretation: Both GUIDs used by Origa2Auth are configured under qcbifbattdrv\AuthLibrary. The matching suggests a shared interface with the Qualcomm BIF battery stack, not an established iris/Hello role. Installed hive records do not prove runtime use.

observations.interpretation: INIT routine invokes the framework table at this slot while constructing WDF driver configuration and object attributes.
PAGE routine passes initialized descriptor/attribute structures and receives a device object.
The path uses typed object context and object reference operations after device creation.
The PAGE routine registers a device interface with this GUID and no reference string. Its consumer is not identified yet.
A second WDF query interface is added using the GUID that the SYSTEM hive labels AuthInterfaceGuid. The query-interface callbacks and consumer are not identified.
The device-add-like path reads and stores this table entry while preparing callback/configuration records; its role in this driver is unresolved.

limits: The slot names match the published KMDF 1.15 function enum and the embedded bind metadata; identifying the device-interface call does not reveal its consumer or establish a biometric role.
This establishes WDF driver/device setup and object-context use, not a biometric match path, credential release, TPM call, secure-world interface, or actual runtime loading.
Callback-record semantics, both interface consumers, IOCTL definitions/consumers, and package binding remain unresolved. Exact public string searches for the recovered GUIDs returned no matches.
No Windows binary was executed and no phone state was changed.
publication: local only; no commit, push, or PR
